rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the highest-uncertainty question is establishing a reliable performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a single modality, single profile, and the most standard/interpretable RNA encoder (PCA). This gives a clean reference accuracy without confounding from aggregation, fusion, or learned encoders. Establishing this floor is critical before investing experiments in more complex multimodal or multiprofile variants, because it tells us (a) whether RNA alone is competitive, (b) the pipeline is functioning correctly, and (c) how much headroom exists for improvements from image, multiprofile aggregation, or fusion. Under a 10-experiment budget, anchoring to the simplest baseline first maximizes the interpretability of all subsequent comparisons.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieved only ~48.5% accuracy, establishing a weak baseline. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is which modality (RNA vs. image) carries the most discriminative signal for this task, as this determines the entire branch of the config space to prioritize over the remaining 8 experiments. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) directly parallels config_001 with the modality swapped, isolating the effect of modality while holding profile setting and aggregation constant. Why: Resolving the modality question early is the highest-leverage decision—if image substantially outperforms RNA, I can focus remaining budget on image encoders and multimodal fusion; if RNA is stronger, I can invest in better RNA encoders (scgpt, scvi) and aggregation; if they are comparable, multimodal fusion becomes the key direction. This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the dominant design axis with a clean, single-variable comparison.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is weak at 20.8%, confirming RNA is the dominant signal. The only RNA encoder tested so far is a linear method (PCA). Question: Does a learned nonlinear RNA representation (scvi_n200) improve over PCA n2000? This experiment (config_004) is a single-variable change from config_001—only the RNA encoder changes—so any accuracy shift can be cleanly attributed to the encoder. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, establishing whether a better RNA representation can push accuracy above ~48% is the highest-leverage question before investing in multiprofile, image, or fusion experiments. If scvi_n200 helps, it justifies further RNA-side exploration (scgpt, multiprofile); if it doesn't, PCA is near-optimal and effort should shift to other axes.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality (0.48-0.52 vs 0.21 for image-only), and scvi_n200 (0.5203) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) by ~3.5%, showing that learned RNA representations matter. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, and it may provide a substantially better or comparable representation. Question: config_007 (scgpt, singleprofile, rna_only) isolates the effect of the RNA encoder while holding profile setting and model setting constant, giving a clean three-way comparison (pca vs scvi vs scgpt). Why this is the best next experiment: Resolving which RNA encoder is strongest is the most fundamental design choice before investing the remaining 6 experiments in multiprofile or multimodal configurations. If scgpt is significantly better, all subsequent experiments should build on it; if it is comparable to or worse than scvi_n200, we confirm scvi as the backbone and can pivot to testing multiprofile or multimodal fusion in the next round. This single experiment reduces the most critical uncertainty at minimal cost.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the best RNA encoder so far (0.5203 acc), clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.4849) and scgpt (0.4106), while image-only resnet50 is very weak (0.2079). We have no data on multiprofile yet. Question: Does multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool) improve on the singleprofile scvi_n200 baseline? This isolates the effect of the profile setting (single→multi) while keeping the encoder fixed at the best-performing one and using the least complex aggregation. Rationale: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming whether multiprofile adds value on the strongest RNA encoder is the highest-information next step. If avgpool helps, we can then test transformer aggregation (config_006) to see if more complex aggregation further helps. If it doesn't, we avoid wasting budget on transformer variants. This is a single-variable change from config_004, making it the cleanest comparison available.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved 0.650 accuracy, a large jump over all singleprofile results, making it the clear current best. The only untested variable within this strong configuration is the aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool). Question: Does transformer aggregation further improve over avgpool for the scvi_n200 multiprofile setup? Why this is the best next step: It is a single-variable change from the current best, cleanly isolating the aggregation effect. The answer directly informs whether to use transformer or avgpool in all remaining multimodal experiments (configs 030-039), making it the highest-information experiment before committing budget to multimodal fusion. With 4 experiments left, resolving this design choice now avoids wasting slots on a suboptimal aggregation in multimodal settings.

Evidence: RNA-only with scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer (config_006, 0.653) is the clear best so far, and multiprofile provides a ~13% boost over single profile. Image alone (resnet50) is very weak (0.208), so it's uncertain whether adding it provides any complementary signal. Question: Does fusing image (resnet50) via concat with the best RNA multiprofile model (scvi_n200, transformer) improve upon the 0.653 RNA-only baseline? This is the highest-value test because it directly probes whether multimodality can push past the current ceiling using the best-known components. Using concat (simpler) and resnet50 (the only image encoder with prior data) keeps the comparison clean. If multimodal helps, the remaining 3 experiments can explore weighted fusion and imagenet_vit_l; if it doesn't, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and conserve budget. This is the best use of experiment 7 because it tests the single most impactful unexplored direction (adding a second modality to the best RNA setup) with minimal confounding variables.

The current best (config_032, acc=0.6878) uses concat fusion in a multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer setup. The only untested axis in this exact configuration is the fusion strategy (weighted vs. concat). Since the image modality alone is weak (resnet50 singleprofile: 0.2079), a weighted fusion could allow the model to down-weight uninformative image features more effectively than a simple concatenation. This is a clean single-variable comparison to the current best, directly testing whether learned modality weighting improves over fixed concatenation. With only 2 experiments remaining after this one, isolating the fusion effect is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step before exploring other axes (e.g., ViT-L image encoder) in the final experiments.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.7131. The strongest remaining uncertainty is whether a more powerful image encoder (imagenet_vit_l vs resnet50) can further improve the multimodal pipeline. Image-only resnet50 was weak (0.208), yet it still contributed meaningfully in the multimodal setting (0.653→0.713), suggesting image quality matters. Config_039 changes exactly one variable from the current best—swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l—while preserving all other winning settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion). This isolates the effect of image representation quality. If it improves, we identify a new best with one experiment left for fine-tuning; if it doesn't, we confirm resnet50 is sufficient and can use the final experiment to probe another axis. This is the highest-information single experiment available under the remaining budget.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250. Evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile as essential, weighted fusion over concat (+0.025), and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (+0.012). The only untested minor variant of this top configuration is swapping transformer aggregation for avgpool while keeping weighted fusion. In RNA-only, transformer vs avgpool made negligible difference (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but in the multimodal setting with a strong image encoder the interaction could differ slightly. Since this is the final experiment, config_037 is the safest exploitation of the current best: it preserves all top-performing components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) and only tests the one remaining untested aggregation variant, giving the best chance of matching or marginally exceeding 0.7250 without risking a large drop from switching to concat fusion.
